players.product: hyperscale data-center leases (>1 MW, 300+ data centers, 1.4 GW under construction) and 0-1 MW colocation / interconnection on PlatformDIGITAL

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matt Mercier sized the capacity runway: 'We have 3 GW of operating capacity today. Behind that, we’ve got 1.4 GW under development', a 50% increase within about two years, and 'After that, we’ve got 7 GW of land capacity' to bring online over the next two to 5+ years. 'That 7 GW of land is in various stages of power procurement. There’s probably almost 3.5-4 GW that we have in hand today in terms of ESAs ready in hand.' He said there has 'never been a better time to be in this industry, but it’s never been probably harder in terms of bringing on power and related capacity'.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 GW operating; 1.4 GW under development; 7 GW of land capacity over two to 5+ years; almost 3.5-4 GW with ESAs in hand

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matt Mercier on agentic / inference demand in the 0-1 MW business: agentic AI is 'still in the early innings', but the last three quarters set records in the 0-1 MW business, and last quarter was a record for interconnections (cross-connects and ServiceFabric), with a record 0-1 MW quarter in EMEA. Deployment sizes are stepping up: a typical 0-1 MW deployment of 300 kW or below is now greater than 500 kW, and 1-5 MW 'is now starting to become more of a standard' for enterprise and service provider customers building inference-oriented architecture. Bulk fiber demand is rising as customers connect training facilities into Digital Realty's interconnected, carrier-heavy campuses.
quarterly_data.figure: typical 0-1 MW deployment from 300 kW or below to greater than 500 kW; 1-5 MW becoming standard; records in 0-1 MW for the last three quarters

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matt Mercier on customer mix and regions: Digital Realty has taken 'a cautious approach' to neocloud exposure (excluding backstop arrangements), picking investment-grade customers, though it has some neocloud exposure, recently in smaller deployments connecting neocloud training workloads through its interconnected gateway facilities. The development pipeline, once mostly in Europe, has shifted to the U.S.; APAC, which 'has been 10% of our portfolio', feels more welcoming to AI and Digital Realty wants to expand there (assets bought in Johor, Malaysia; deals across Japan). The company has 6,000 customers in over 50 markets.
quarterly_data.figure: APAC 10% of portfolio; 6,000 customers; over 50 markets

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Matt Mercier on pricing and growth: with a broad supply-demand imbalance, pricing continues to pick up across the majority of Digital Realty's global markets, seen in new signings, development yields and renewal spreads, and expiring rents over the next couple of years sit on a downward trajectory versus market. He reiterated 10% bottom-line growth, 'which we’ve done last year, we expect to do this year, and expect to continue that for several years to come'.
quarterly_data.figure: 10% bottom-line growth expected this year and for several years
